case_title: Ashwani Kumar Saxena v. State of M.P.
previous_criminal_record: Yes, involved in few other criminal cases
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.27
neutral_facts: The accused, along with two others, were charged with murder and attempted murder for an incident that resulted in the death of a victim. The accused claimed to be a juvenile at the time of the incident, providing school records to support his age. The trial court and appellate court rejected the school records, relying on medical evidence to determine the accused's age. The accused was found to be over 18 years old at the time of the incident, leading to a conviction for life imprisonment. However, the Supreme Court held that the procedure followed by the lower courts was incorrect, as the age determination should have been conducted under the Juvenile Justice Act, not through medical tests. The Supreme Court set aside the conviction and directed the case to be reviewed by the Juvenile Justice Board.
